$comment: Upload variants. Each is a prefab variant of the root avatar prefab (or of the variant it `extends`) with feature prefabs added as children; `features` lists the ones the generator makes sure are present. Slugs are the names the avatar is uploaded under. `about` is for whoever reads this file and is not sent anywhere. Features whose package is not installed are skipped with a warning. `worstRank` is the worst VRChat performance rank the variant may build to on PC and `worstRankMobile` on Android and iOS; the checks fail if it ranks lower. `model` is the fidelity level a variant is built from: left out, the full model on PC and the lite one on Android and iOS; "lite", the lite one everywhere. `platforms` (pc, android, ios; all three when left out) says what the variant is built for. `wardrobe` names another set of clothes the variant is built wearing: Blender exports each wardrobe as a model of its own on the same skeleton (BlenderExports/cass-<wardrobe>.fbx and its -lite), and the build exchanges the meshes by name. Features that cannot work on mobile say so themselves and are left out of those builds. `local` lists prefabs a variant adds that are not in the repository, each by the GUID its author shipped it with, with the name, author and address it is credited by; `atView` stands it at the avatar's view position. They are bought assets whose terms forbid passing them on. A variant with any is only made, built or uploaded in a project where all of them have been imported (every command skips it elsewhere and says why), its description credits them, and it uploads private and without the licence tag.
description: Cassidy's avatar. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar Body: SiroinoSotai by Siroino. Face: Mizunashi Hiyori by HENGE.

variants.about: Everyday build: default outfit, weighty locomotion baked for this avatar's own skeleton (scripts/cass.sh gaits), face tracking, and a crash while away: the body locks, the mesh glitches, the eyes go to an error screen and a window reading AFK stands beside it.
The everyday build from the low-polygon model, for PC as well: the same avatar and features at well under half the triangles.
Adventure build: adds flight, a stepladder for a lifted play space, a carry seat, a catch-up portal and the hand tools.

The adventure build for leading a group: its laser pointer can ping the spot it points at, a beacon marks the wearer through walls and points other people's view towards them, and there are seats to put down, in a ring or facing a screen. The ping's marker, the beacon and the seats are meshes of their own, which takes it past Good, hence a variant of its own.
The everyday build with the party tricks: a bonk hammer, the vanishing act, the mosaic censor and the busy sign.

The everyday build that changes its outfit whenever a viewer looks away from it and back. Each viewer's client rolls for itself, so nothing is synced and no two people need see the same outfit. The outfits are UV tiles, which mobile shaders cannot hide, so it is built for PC only.
The everyday build with the shape collector: a collect-the-shapes course to lay out in any world. The course is a skinned mesh of its own, a third, which is Medium on PC.

The adventure build with one real light source: the flashlight, a spotlight, which can be left standing in the world. It replaces both of cass-adv's glowing stand-ins. Any light on an avatar ranks it Poor and a second Very Poor, hence one light and a variant of its own.

The adventure build with one real light source: the lantern, a point light, which can be left standing in the world. It replaces both of cass-adv's glowing stand-ins. Any light on an avatar ranks it Poor and a second Very Poor, hence one light and a variant of its own.

A sampler for choosing how the avatar walks: the root avatar with every walk style of the locomotion package baked for it, and a Walk style menu to switch between them in game. It does not extend cass, whose own locomotion would be a second claim on the same playable layers. Its controllers are large and are not committed; scripts/cass.sh gaits styles writes them. PC only: it is for trying on, and the choice is made once.

The everyday build in the cyber wardrobe: a techwear jacket, a utility vest, a pleated skirt with a lit hem, chunky boots and a headset in place of the hat. The same avatar, skeleton and switches; only the clothes differ, and they are exchanged by mesh name at build time like the low-polygon model.

The everyday build carrying Quick Hack by DiNe Shop, a bought prop. The prop is not in the repository: its terms do not allow passing it on, or uploading it where others could clone it. So this variant can only be made where its package has been imported (see `local`), and it uploads private. PC only, as the prop is.

The everyday build with everything from net.wirenook.contacts, for trying VRChat's standard contact tags with someone: it reacts to being touched by them, and carries the tester that emits each one and launches things, the shield that burns and the targets to set down. One avatar to clone for both halves of a test.
